meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: Humble 1st person plural pronoun used when speaking to superiors or in formal settings.

examples.trans: We will prepare first.
Welcome to our company.
Did you hear about this cast member?
I was busy today because of cast member.
Did you hear about this sudden cancellation?
I was busy today because of sudden cancellation.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Describes physical or mental tiredness.

examples.text: 어제 잠을 못 자서 너무 피곤해요.
examples.trans: I couldn't sleep yesterday, so I'm really tired.
If you're tired, please rest a bit.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?
Oh, wow, nice to meet you!
Oh, wow, I understand now.
The atmosphere today is really plucky, spirited.
That person always looks plucky, spirited.
Did you hear about this to my liking?
I was busy today because of to my liking.

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.
If it's heavy, I'll carry it.

meanings.note: Used to draw attention or start an action

examples.trans: Alright, let's begin!
Here you go.
There are fifty thousand here.
Altogether, it is fifty thousand people.

meanings.note: Bound noun used with Sino-Korean numbers to state prices in South Korean won.

examples.trans: I only have a thousand won.
That is ten thousand won in total.
Thank you for helping.
Yes, that's right.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!
Did you hear about this sweet filled pancakes?
I was busy today because of sweet filled pancakes.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Past tense is 샀다 / 샀어요.

examples.trans: I bought fruit at the mart.
I need to buy a birthday present for my friend.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Short for 아침밥

examples.trans: I woke up early in the morning.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?
The atmosphere today is really feel peckish.
That person always looks feel peckish.
There are five here.
Altogether, it is five people.

meanings.note: General-purpose counter noun used with native Korean determiners (한 개, 두 개, 세 개).

examples.trans: How many do you need?
I bought three loaves of bread.
Did you hear about this green tea?
I was busy today because of green tea.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
